constraints.aca_description_paragraph_1: 'About 2 years ago a young man left home. He had not been heard from until October, when his mother received the enciphered message traced above. It has been forwarded to us [the ACA] for help in reading it.'
constraints.aca_description_paragraph_2: envelope typed correctly except a lowercase 'a' in 'Apt.' and in 'Avienda'/'Avenida'; return address read only 'Milestone' (parents believed this hinted at 'passed a milestone' in his life); message written in ballpoint pen on a strip of paper torn/cut from a larger sheet; MLH are the mother's initials; 'no hint as to why he wrote in cipher; he had not shown any interest in cryptography that they know of'
constraints.aca_description_paragraph_3: author born 19 Nov 1954; former programmer and electronic circuit designer; badly injured in an industrial accident, recovered, then injured again in an auto accident that killed two friends; interested in American history before the accidents, then in parapsychology, religion and astrology afterward
constraints.aca_description_paragraph_4: only other trace: a cashed check in Paris the previous February; seems to have disposed of possessions, returning items to friends; message sent from Israel by air mail
constraints.reading_direction_hypothesis: commenter Wolfgang Wilhelm: since sent from Israel, consider the note may have been written right-to-left
constraints.rebus_hypothesis: commenter Richard SantaColoma: possible rebus reading, e.g. a caret as 'greater than', a circle/dot as 'eye', a heart with plus/minus as 'more or less love' -- speculative, not a proposed full solution
constraints.computer_symbol_hypothesis: commenter Richard SantaColoma, given the sender's programming/circuit-design background: several symbols resemble ALGOL68, APL and early C language characters, some of which map directly to specific IBM keyboard keys
constraints.aca_outcome: Tobias Schrodel contacted the ACA directly asking if anything new had been found since 1976; 'apparently, this was not the case'
constraints.null_hypothesis: Schmeh himself notes the symbols could be meaningless, deliberately sent to confuse the parents -- 'this hypothesis is hard to prove'
